assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Uniform velocity
items.clue: Motion at the same speed in the same direction.

items.label: Deceleration
items.clue: The rate at which the velocity of a vehicle decreases.

items.label: Braking distance
items.clue: How far the vehicle travels while it is being slowed to rest.

items.label: Newton's Third Law
items.clue: When two objects interact, the forces they exert on each other are equal and opposite.

questions.stem: A book lies at rest on a table. Which statement about the forces on the book is correct?

options.text: There are no forces on the book while it lies still.
The table's push must be bigger, to hold the book up.
Its weight and the table's push give a resultant of zero.
The book's weight is bigger, but the table is far too solid.

questions.explanation: Two forces act on the book, downward weight and the table's upward push; they are equal and opposite, so the resultant force on the book is zero.

questions.stem: In the equation resultant force = mass x acceleration, which set of units must be used?

options.text: force in newtons, N; mass in kilograms, kg; acceleration in m/s
force in newtons, N; mass in grams, g; acceleration in m/s^2
force in kilograms, mass in newtons, acceleration in m/s^2
force in newtons, N; mass in kilograms, kg; acceleration in m/s^2

questions.explanation: The specification gives force, F, in newtons, N; mass, m, in kilograms, kg; and acceleration, a, in metres per second squared, m/s^2.

questions.stem: (Physics only) A car is driven at 13 m/s, a typical speed in a built-up area. The driver's reaction time is about 0.7 s, and the braking distance at this speed is about 14 m. Estimate the distance the car needs to make an emergency stop.

options.text: About 14 m, which is the braking distance
About 9 m, covered while the driver reacts
About 18 m: twice the thinking distance
About 23 m: 9 m thinking, 14 m braking

questions.stem: A driver holds a long hands-free phone conversation while driving. What does the specification say about this?

options.text: It has no effect, as the driver's hands stay on the wheel
Distractions may also affect a driver's ability to react
It lengthens the braking distance, not the thinking one
It matters only if the driver is also tired or drunk

questions.explanation: The specification states that distractions may also affect a driver's ability to react. A slower reaction means a longer thinking distance and so a longer stopping distance.

questions.stem: Heavy rain begins during a motorway journey. Which action best reflects the physics of stopping distance, and why?

options.text: Slow down and leave a bigger gap, as braking needs more road
Keep the same gap, since the reaction time is unchanged
Brake as hard as possible each time, to stop sooner
Drive faster, to spend less time out in the rain

questions.explanation: Wet conditions reduce grip and so lengthen the braking distance, while the thinking distance is unchanged. Driving more slowly and leaving a larger gap restores the safety margin.

questions.stem: A lorry driver brakes heavily and repeatedly on a long, steep hill. What is the most likely consequence, and why?

options.text: The brakes cool down, as the lorry is slowing
The brakes overheat, so they become less effective
The kinetic energy of the lorry rises as it descends
The kinetic energy is stored in the brakes

questions.explanation: Work done by the friction force raises the temperature of the brakes. Repeated heavy braking gives them no chance to cool, and overheated brakes lose their effectiveness.

questions.stem: Why is acceleration measured in metres per second squared, m/s^2?

options.text: A change of velocity in m/s is divided by a time in s.
A distance in metres is divided by a time in seconds twice.
A velocity in m/s is multiplied by the time taken.
The object covers a squared distance each second.

questions.explanation: Acceleration is a velocity change divided by the time it takes, so its unit is m/s divided by s, which is written m/s^2.

questions.stem: (Physics only) A graph shows stopping distance on the vertical axis against speed on the horizontal axis for a family car. What shape is the line, and why?

options.text: A curve that gets steeper, as braking distance grows fastest
A straight line through the origin, as distance = speed
A straight line sloping steadily upward
A horizontal line, because the braking force is fixed

questions.explanation: The thinking distance contribution is a straight line through the origin, but the braking distance contribution rises with speed squared, so the total curves upwards ever more steeply.

questions.stem: In the ruler drop test one student holds a ruler above a partner's open hand, releases it without warning, and the partner catches it as quickly as they can. Which measurement is taken, and what is done with it?

options.text: The time in seconds is read directly from the ruler scale
The number of centimetres is used as the time in seconds
The drop distance is measured, then converted to a time
The mass of the ruler is used to find the time of fall

questions.stem: On a dry road a car travelling at 31 m/s (about 70 mph) has a stopping distance of roughly 96 m, of which about 22 m is thinking distance. Estimate its stopping distance at the same speed on a wet road.

options.text: About 96 m, because the driver reacts just as quickly
About 170 m, since the braking part roughly doubles
About 48 m, as water lubricates the road well
About 31 m, one metre for each metre per second

questions.explanation: The thinking distance of about 22 m is unchanged, but the braking distance of about 74 m roughly doubles on a wet surface, taking the total to somewhere near 170 m.

questions.stem: A family car reaches a speed of about 27 m/s from rest in about 9 s. Estimate its acceleration.

options.text: ~3 m/s^2, from a gain of about 27 m/s in about 9 s
~27 m/s^2, the speed the car reaches on the road
~240 m/s^2, from 27 m/s multiplied by the 9 s
~9 m/s^2, the same as free fall near the Earth

questions.explanation: Dividing the change of velocity by the time gives 27 / 9 = 3, so the acceleration is about 3 m/s^2, quoted as an approximate value.

questions.stem: (Physics only) Stopping distance is plotted against speed for a car and for a fully loaded lorry. At every speed shown the lorry's line lies above the car's line, and the gap between them widens as speed increases. What does the graph show?

options.text: The lorry driver has a longer reaction time than the car driver
The lorry needs a longer stopping distance at every speed
The lorry is always driven faster than the car is driven
Both lines are straight, so distance doubles with speed
